title: Releases · bastillion-io/Bastillion
excerpt: Bastillion gives you a clean, browser-based way to manage SSH access across all your systems—like a bastion host with a friendly dashboard. - bastillion-io/Bastillion
content_html:
5.1.0

🎬 Session audit & replay — now a first-class feature, on by default

Every terminal session is now recorded and can be replayed from Audit Sessions in the
UI — who ran what, where, and when, side by side for sessions that spanned multiple hosts,
with a text filter to jump straight to the lines that matter.

This feature existed behind enableInternalAudit but was experimental: reviewing a session
loaded its entire output into the browser in one shot, which hung the tab on any session
with real output. That's fixed properly:

  • Output streams from the database to the browser and renders incrementally — sessions
    with hundreds of megabytes of terminal output replay without breaking a sweat
  • Fixed a server-side cleanup loop that was quadratic in session size and could spin a
    request thread forever when output contained a backspace at the start of a line
  • Full ANSI/VT100 control sequences (colors, cursor movement, screen modes, window titles)
    are now stripped from replayed output — no more [?1049h noise from top and friends

Practically every compliance framework has a privileged-access audit-trail requirement
somewhere — PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001 — and this checks that box without a
commercial PAM product.

Upgrade note: enableInternalAudit now defaults to true on fresh installs; existing
installs keep whatever their persisted config says. Retention is deleteAuditLogAfter
(90 days by default); disable recording entirely with ENABLE_INTERNAL_AUDIT=false. If you
scripted against the old getJSONTermOutputForSession.ktrl endpoint, it's replaced by the
streaming streamTermOutputForSession.ktrl (plain text, one line per record).

🔒 Hardening

  • CSRF token comparison is now constant-time

📦 Dependencies

  • Bouncy Castle bcprov-jdk18on 1.84 → 1.85
  • JUnit Jupiter 6.1.1 → 6.1.2

5.0.0

Highlights

  • Licensing model — Bastillion now runs unlicensed at up to 5 registered systems.
    Paid tiers (Starter/Team/Business) raise the cap; a .lic file is supplied via the
    LICENSE_KEY env var or licenseKey in BastillionConfig.properties. New
    LicenseUtil validates the license, enforces the system cap, and surfaces
    licensee/expiry info (with a 90-day pre-expiry warning) under Settings.
  • Self-contained jar — the app now runs as java -jar with an embedded Jetty
    server and HTTPS out of the box (new io.bastillion.Main), instead of requiring a
    separate servlet container distribution.
  • Upgraded to Java 21 and Jakarta EE 11, with dependency updates across the board.
  • Full Ed25519 (default) and Ed448 SSH key support.
  • v4 → v5 migration tool (tools/migrate) — a standalone export/import utility
    that moves users, systems, profiles, scripts, public keys, audit logs, and the
    Bastillion application SSH key/identity from a v4 H2 database into a fresh v5
    instance, re-encrypting secrets under the new instance's keystore. See
    tools/migrate/README.md for the full procedure.

Security

  • New SecurityHeadersFilter adds hardened response headers app-wide.
  • New CSRFFilter (part of the bundled MVC framework) protects state-changing
    requests.
  • Session cookies now set secure in addition to the existing http-only.
  • EncryptionUtil and KeyStoreUtil were reworked; AuthDB/password verification
    now supports the newer PBKDF2 hash format alongside the legacy single-round
    SHA-256 formats (including v4's own concatenation scheme), so users can migrate
    and log in with existing passwords unchanged.

Internal / build

  • The previously external io.bastillion:lmvc framework dependency is now merged
    directly into the codebase as loophole.mvc, so the whole app builds from one
    pom.xml.
  • Added unit test coverage: AppConfigTest, EncryptionUtilTest, LicenseUtilTest,
    and new tests for the loophole.mvc framework (dispatcher, base controller, CSRF
    and security filters).
  • CI (.github/workflows/github-build.yml) now runs the build/test on every push
    and pull request, in addition to the existing hourly schedule — previously it
    only ran on cron, so commits weren't verified until the next scheduled run.
  • README overhauled with an updated feature walkthrough, licensing section, and
    screenshots.

Upgrading from v4

Use tools/migrate to bring your data forward — see tools/migrate/README.md.
Password hashes migrate as-is; existing users can log in immediately without a
reset.

4.0.1

🚀 Bastillion Release Notes

What’s New

  • ✅ Upgraded to Java 21 and Jakarta EE 11 — modern language features, improved performance, and long-term support.
  • 🔐 Added full support for Ed25519 and Ed448 SSH key generation, with Ed25519 now set as the default key type.
  • 📦 Updated all libraries and dependencies to their latest stable releases for enhanced security, stability, and compatibility.

Migration Guide (from v3.10.00)

To migrate from a previous installation:

  1. Ensure Java 21 is installed
    Bastillion now requires Java 21. Confirm it's installed and available in your environment:

    java --version

    On Ubuntu, you can install it via:

    sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y openjdk‑21‑jdk

  2. Backup your existing database
    The H2 data store is usually named:

    bastillion.h2.db

    (Older versions may use keybox.h2.db.)

  3. Copy the following files and directories from your old installation:

    • jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/keydb/ → copy the entire folder and its contents
    • jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/bastillion.jceks
    • jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/BastillionConfig.properties

  4. Review and migrate configuration files as needed:

    • jaas.conf
    • log4j2.xml
    • keystore
    • jetty-ssl.xml
    • jetty-http.xml

  5. Restart Bastillion
    Confirm that the application is connected to its previous database and that all services start cleanly under Jetty.

Additional Notes

  • Ed25519 keys (256-bit) are now the default for improved speed and security.
  • Ed448 keys (448-bit) are supported for environments requiring extended cryptographic strength.
  • Migration preserves existing authorized keys and stored credentials if configuration paths are copied correctly.

3.15.00

Update 3rd party dependencies to latest including Jetty.

To migrate from >= 3.10.00

  • Backup previous bastillion.h2.db data store (possibly named keybox.h2.db)
  • Copy old jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/keydb folder (and it's contents) to the jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes directory of the new installation.
  • Copy old jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/bastillion.jceks to the /jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes directory of the new installation.
  • Copy old jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/BastillionConfig.properties to the /jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes directory of the new installation.
  • Run the bastillion-upgrade-4.00.01.jar on the database copied to the new installation
java -jar bastillion-upgrade-4.00.01.jar /jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/BastillionConfig.properties
  • Adjust settings or copy as needed for the jaas.conf, log4j2.xml, keystore, jetty-ssl.xml and jetty-http.xml

5.1.0

🎬 会话审核和重放 — 现在是一流功能，默认开启

现在，每个终端会话都会被记录下来，并且可以从 UI 中的审核会话中重播 — 谁在何时、何地运行了哪些内容，对于跨多个主机的会话并排运行，并使用文本过滤器直接跳转到重要的行。

此功能存在于enableInternalAudit背后，但只是实验性的：检查会话将其整个输出一次性加载到浏览器中，这将选项卡挂在具有真实输出的任何会话上。 已正确修复：

  • 输出从数据库流式传输到浏览器并增量渲染 — 会话具有数百兆字节的终端输出重放，无需费力
  • 修复了服务器端清理循环，该循环的会话大小呈二次方，并且当输出在行开头包含退格键时可能会永远旋转请求线程
  • 完整的 ANSI/VT100 控制序列（颜色、光标移动、屏幕模式、窗口标题）现在已从重播输出中删除 — 不再有来自顶部和朋友的 [?1049h 噪音

实际上，每个合规性框架在某些地方都有特权访问审计跟踪要求 - PCI DSS、HIPAA、SOC 2、ISO 27001 - 并且无需商业 PAM 产品即可检查该框。

升级说明：enableInternalAudit 现在在全新安装时默认为 true；现有安装保留其持久配置所说的任何内容。 保留期为deleteAuditLogAfter（默认90天）；使用 ENABLE_INTERNAL_AUDIT=false 完全禁用记录。 如果您针对旧的 getJSONTermOutputForSession.ktrl 端点编写脚本，它将被流式streamTermOutputForSession.ktrl（纯文本，每条记录一行）替换。

🔒 硬化

  • CSRF 令牌比较现在是恒定时间的

📦 依赖关系

  • Bouncy Castle bcprov-jdk18on 1.84 → 1.85
  • JUnit 木星 6.1.1 → 6.1.2

5.0.0

亮点

  • 许可模型——Bastillion 现在无需许可即可在最多 5 个注册系统上运行。 付费等级（新手/团队/商业）提高了上限； .lic 文件是通过 BastilionConfig.properties 中的 LICENSE_KEY 环境变量或 licenseKey 提供的。 新的 LicenseUtil 会验证许可证、强制执行系统上限，并在“设置”下显示被许可人/到期信息（带有 90 天到期前警告）。
  • 自包含的 jar — 该应用程序现在作为 java -jar 运行，带有嵌入式 Jetty 服务器和开箱即用的 HTTPS（新 io.bastillion.Main），而不需要单独的 servlet 容器分发。
  • 升级到 Java 21 和 Jakarta EE 11，全面更新依赖项。
  • 完整的 Ed25519（默认）和 Ed448 SSH 密钥支持。
  • v4 → v5 迁移工具 (tools/migrate) — 一个独立的导出/导入实用程序，可将用户、系统、配置文件、脚本、公钥、审核日志和 Bastilion 应用程序 SSH 密钥/身份从 v4 H2 数据库移动到新的 v5 实例，并在新实例的密钥库下重新加密机密。 有关完整过程，请参阅tools/migrate/README.md。

安全

  • 新的 SecurityHeadersFilter 在应用程序范围内添加了强化的响应标头。
  • 新的 CSRFFilter（捆绑的 MVC 框架的一部分）可保护状态更改请求。
  • 除了现有的仅 http 之外，会话 cookie 现在也设置为安全的。
  • EncryptionUtil 和 KeyStoreUtil 进行了重新设计； AuthDB/密码验证现在支持较新的 PBKDF2 哈希格式以及传统的单轮 SHA-256 格式（包括 v4 自己的串联方案），因此用户可以在现有密码不变的情况下迁移和登录。

内部/构建

  • 之前的外部 io.bastillion:lmvc 框架依赖项现在作为 loophole.mvc 直接合并到代码库中，因此整个应用程序都是从一个 pom.xml 构建的。
  • 添加了单元测试覆盖范围：AppConfigTest、EncryptionUtilTest、LicenseUtilTest 以及针对loophole.mvc 框架（调度程序、基本控制器、CSRF 和安全过滤器）的新测试。
  • CI (.github/workflows/github-build.yml) 现在除了现有的每小时计划外，还对每个推送和拉取请求运行构建/测试 - 以前它仅在 cron 上运行，因此直到下一次计划运行时才会验证提交。
  • 对自述文件进行了彻底修改，更新了功能演练、许可部分和屏幕截图。

从 v4 升级

使用tools/migrate 来推进数据 — 请参阅tools/migrate/README.md。 密码哈希按原样迁移；现有用户无需重置即可立即登录。

迁移指南（v3.10.00 起）

要从以前的安装迁移：

  1. 确保已安装 Java 21 Basstillion 现在需要 Java 21。 确认它已安装并在您的环境中可用： java --version 在 Ubuntu 上，您可以通过以下方式安装它： sudo apt update sudo apt install -y openjdk‑21‑jdk
  2. 备份现有数据库 H2 数据存储通常命名为：bastillion.h2.db（旧版本可能使用 keybox.h2.db。）
  3. 从旧安装中复制以下文件和目录： jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/keydb/ → 复制整个文件夹及其内容 jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/bastillion.jceks jetty/bastillion/WEB-INF/classes/BastillionConfig.properties

  5. 重新启动 Bastilion 确认应用程序已连接到其先前的数据库，并且所有服务在 Jetty 下干净启动。

  • Ed25519 密钥（256 位）现在是默认密钥，以提高速度和安全性。
